fieldMapping.note: Stripe session id, used as Idempotency-Key to prevent duplicate creations
Optional Stripe client reference ID, mapped to a custom HubSpot property if needed

assumptions: The Stripe webhook payload includes the 'email' field for the customer.
The HubSpot integration uses the contact's email as the unique identifier for create-or-update operations.
The Stripe session id will be passed as the Idempotency-Key in the HTTP request header to HubSpot to ensure idempotency.
No additional HubSpot property mapping is required beyond the standard email property unless a custom mapping is specified.

Retrieve a Checkout Session | Stripe API Reference
Create or update a contact by email - HubSpot docs

notes: The source is a webhook; the connector must expose a POST endpoint to receive Stripe webhook events.
Stripe webhook payloads include the full Checkout Session object under the 'data.object' key.
The email field is located at data.object.customer_email.
The session ID is at data.object.id.
The client_reference_id is at data.object.client_reference_id and may be null.
The connector must verify the webhook signature using the Stripe signing secret (not shown in docs but required for security).
The contact_email path parameter must be URL-encoded if it contains special characters.
The request body must be a JSON object with a 'properties' array containing objects with 'property' and 'value' keys.
To enforce idempotency using the Stripe session ID, the connector should include the Stripe session ID in the 'Idempotency-Key' HTTP header (not shown in HubSpot docs but supported by the API).
If the contact does not exist, it will be created; if it exists, it will be updated with the provided properties.
Only the email property is required in the properties array for this operation; additional properties can be included as needed.
The HubSpot API version used here is v1 Legacy; consider using v3 (/crm/v3/objects/contacts) for newer features, but the v1 endpoint is sufficient for createOrUpdate by email.
